There were ten more truth-tellers than liars in a room. Everyone in the room was asked, "Are you a truth-teller?" and everyone gave an answer. A total of 20 people answered, "Yes." How many liars were in the room?

Five circles, each with an area of $8\ \text{cm}^2$, overlap each other to form the figure shown. The area of each section where two circles overlap is $1\ \text{cm}^2$. What is the total area covered by the figure?

solutions.title: Subtract the double counting
solutions.body:
If the circles did not overlap, the total area would be $5\times8=40\ \text{cm}^2$. Each of the four overlapping regions has been counted twice, so subtract each once: $40-4\times1=36\ \text{cm}^2$.

**Answer: (B) $36\ \text{cm}^2$**

prompt: Ria has some £1 coins and some £2 coins in her pocket. She has 50% more £1 coins than £2 coins. She has £35 in total. How many £2 coins does Ria have?

solutions.title: Use groups
solutions.body:
If Ria has $2x$ £2 coins then she has $3x$ £1 coins (50% more). The total is $3x\times1+2x\times2=7x=35$, so $x=5$ and she has $2x=10$ £2 coins.

**Answer: (B) 10**

solutions.title: Check the answer
solutions.body:
Try 10 two-pound coins: £20, and 15 one-pound coins: £15. The total is £35 and $15=1.5\times10$. ✓

**Answer: (B) 10**

Eddie wants to write a number in each circle in the diagram. He wants each number to be equal to the sum of the numbers in the two adjacent circles. He has already written two numbers, as shown. What number should he write in the grey circle?

solutions.title: Go round the ring
solutions.body:
Name the empty circles going round: the top circle $p$, then (clockwise) the circle next to 2 is $s$, the grey bottom circle is $r$, and the circle next to 1 is $q$.

The top circle is between the circles with 1 and 2, so $p=1+2=3$. The circle with 1 is between $p$ and $q$, so $1=3+q$ and $q=-2$. The circle with 2 is between $p$ and $s$, so $2=3+s$ and $s=-1$. The grey circle is between $q$ and $s$, so it holds $-2+(-1)=-3$.

**Answer: (D) $-3$**

prompt: Werner is on a treadmill in the gym. He keeps looking at two stopwatches. The first shows the time elapsed since he started and the second the time remaining until the end of his session. At some point during the session they show 14:58 (elapsed) and 21:32 (remaining). What time do the stopwatches show when they display the same times?

Julia wants to fill in each box with a different prime number less than 20 so that the value of $X=\dfrac{\square+\square+\square+\square+\square+\square+\square}{\square}$ is an integer. (Seven boxes are added in the numerator and one box is the denominator.) What is the maximum possible value of $X$?

solutions.title: The denominator must divide 77
solutions.body:
The eight primes below 20 are $2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19$, with sum $77$. All eight boxes get a different prime, so if the denominator is $Y$ the numerator is $77-Y$ and $X=\dfrac{77-Y}{Y}=\dfrac{77}{Y}-1$.

For $X$ to be an integer, $Y$ must divide $77=7\times11$, so $Y=7$ or $Y=11$. The larger value of $X$ comes from the smaller $Y$: $X=\dfrac{77}{7}-1=10$.

**Answer: (C) 10**

prompt: The integers $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ satisfy $a<2b$, $b<3c$, $c<4d$ and $d<100$. What is the largest possible value of $a$?

solutions.title: Work backwards from d
solutions.body:
Since the numbers are integers, $d<100$ gives $d\le99$. Then $c<4d\le396$, so $c\le395$. Then $b<3c\le1185$, so $b\le1184$. Finally $a<2b\le2368$, so $a\le2367$, and this value is achieved by $d=99,\ c=395,\ b=1184,\ a=2367$.

**Answer: (C) 2367**

prompt: In the rectangle $PQRS$, the points $T$ and $U$ are marked on side $SR$ as shown, so that $\angle RUQ=\angle STP=45^\circ$ and $PQ+UT=20$ cm. What is the length of $QR$?

Sanja has two bowls of numbered balls. Bowl X contains seven balls numbered 1, 2, 6, 7, 10, 11 and 12. Bowl Y contains five balls numbered 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9. Which ball should Sanja transfer from Bowl X to Bowl Y to increase the mean of the numbers on the balls in each bowl?

solutions.title: Compare with the current means
solutions.body:
Bowl X has total $1+2+6+7+10+11+12=49$, so its mean is $49\div7=7$. Bowl Y has total $29$ and mean $29\div5=5.8$.

Removing a ball raises the mean of X only if the ball is below 7, and adding a ball raises the mean of Y only if the ball is above 5.8. The only ball in X that is below 7 and above 5.8 is 6.

**Answer: (E) 6**

During two sessions of football training, Paul shoots a total of 17 times at a target. He hits with 60% of his shots in the first session. He hits with 75% of his shots in the second session. How many times did he hit the target in the second session?

Anurag leaves for school at 8:00 a.m. His school is 1 km away. When he walks, his speed is 4 km/h. When he cycles, his speed is 15 km/h. He is 5 minutes early when he walks. How many minutes early is he when he cycles?

Jaina is a train driver. She drives the train from Sao Paolo to Rio. The journey usually takes 4 hours, non-stop and at constant speed. One day, the train stopped half way for 40 minutes. By what percentage did Jaina then need to increase the train's speed to still arrive on time?

solutions.title: Compare the times for the second half
solutions.body:
The second half normally takes 2 hours $=120$ minutes. After a 40-minute stop, the second half must be done in $120-40=80$ minutes.

Speed is inversely proportional to time for the same distance, so the new speed is $\dfrac{120}{80}=1.5$ times the old speed, an increase of 50%.

**Answer: (C) 50**

solutions.title: Use numbers
solutions.body:
Say the whole trip is 240 km, so the speed is 60 km/h. The second half is 120 km and must take $1\tfrac{1}{3}$ hours, needing $120\div\tfrac43=90$ km/h. That is 30 km/h more than 60, i.e. 50% more.

**Answer: (C) 50**

Adira keeps gold, red, black, pink and white pearls in five small boxes. Each box contains pearls of only one colour. The boxes are labelled A: "gold or red", B: "pink or black", C: "black or gold", D: "not black", E: "pink or white", and all the statements are true. Adira's friend Lilly wants to know which box contains the gold pearls. She may open exactly one of the five boxes to look inside. Which box must Lilly open to be certain which of the boxes contains the gold pearls?

solutions.title: Open box D
solutions.body:
If D holds gold, she has found it. If D holds red, then A (gold or red) holds gold. If D holds pink, then B (pink or black) holds black, so C (black or gold) holds gold. If D holds white, then E (pink or white) holds pink, so B holds black, and again C holds gold. So opening D always settles it.

Other boxes can fail. For example, if Lilly opens A and sees red, the boxes B, C, D, E could hold (pink, black, gold, white), (black, gold, pink, white) or (black, gold, white, pink); in the first D holds gold and in the others C does, so she cannot tell. (Boxes B, C and E can be shown not to work in a similar way.)

**Answer: (D)**

prompt: Some birds, including Ha, Long, Nha and Trang, are perching on four parallel wires which are one above the other. There are 10 birds perched above Ha. There are 25 birds perched above Long. There are five birds perched below Nha. There are two birds perched below Trang. The number of birds perched above Trang is a multiple of the number of birds perched below her. How many birds in total are perched on the four wires?

solutions.title: Locate the four birds
solutions.body:
Call the wires W, X, Y, Z from the top. Neither Ha nor Long can be on W (some bird is above each). Neither Nha nor Trang can be on Z. Long has more birds above than Ha, so Long is on a lower wire than Ha. Nha has 5 below and Trang has 2 below, so Nha is on a higher wire than Trang.

Suppose Nha were on W. Every bird on W is above Ha (Ha is not on W), so W holds at most 10 birds. The birds not below Nha are exactly those on W, so the total would be at most $10+5=15$. But Long has 25 birds above, so there are at least 26 birds. Contradiction. So Nha is on X and Trang on Y.

Long is on Y or Z. If Long were on Y with Trang, Trang would have 25 birds above and 2 below, but 25 is not a multiple of 2. So Long is on Z, which holds only the 2 birds below Trang, including Long.

The total is the 25 above Long plus the 2 on Z (Long and one other): $25+2=27$.

**Answer: (A) 27**
